arxiv-2108-03819.title: DistillPose: Lightweight Camera Localization Using Auxiliary Learning
arxiv-2108-03819.creator: Yehya Abouelnaga, Mai Bui, Slobodan Ilic
arxiv-2108-03819.description: Abstract We propose a lightweight retrieval-based pipeline to predict 6DOF camera poses from RGB images. Our pipeline uses a convolutional neural network (CNN) to encode a query image as a feature vector. A nearest neighbor lookup finds the pose-wise nearest database image.

arxiv-2109-10090.title: Triangle mechanism in the decay process J / ψ → K − ​ K + ​ a 1 ​ ( 1260 ) J/\psi\to K^{-}K^{+}a_{1}(1260)
arxiv-2109-10090.creator: Xuan Luo, Dazhuang He, Yiling Xie, Hao Sun
arxiv-2109-10090.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Xuan Luo, Dazhuang He, Yiling Xie, Hao Sun. The role of triangle mechanism in the decay process J / ψ → K − ​ K + ​ a 1 ​ ( 1260 ) J/\psi\to K^{-}K^{+}a_{1}(1260) is probed.

arxiv-2111-03938.title: Improved Lieb–Thirring type inequalities for non-selfadjoint Schrödinger operators
arxiv-2111-03938.creator: Sabine Bögli
arxiv-2111-03938.description: Abstract . We improve the Lieb–Thirring type inequalities by Demuth, Hansmann and Katriel (J. Funct. Anal. 2009) for Schrödinger operators with complex-valued potentials. Our result involves a positive, integrable function. We show that in the one-dimensional case the result is sharp in the sense that if we take a non-integrable function, then an analogous inequality cannot hold.

arxiv-2203-12967.title: Extended critical regimes of deep neural networks DOI: www.pnas.org/cgi/doi/10.1073/pnas.XXXXXXXXXX
arxiv-2203-12967.creator: Cheng Kevin Qu, Asem Wardak, Pulin Gong
arxiv-2203-12967.description: Abstract Deep neural networks (DNNs) have been successfully applied to many real-world problems, but a complete understanding of their dynamical and computational principles is still lacking. Conventional theoretical frameworks for analysing DNNs often assume random networks with coupling weights obeying Gaussian statistics. However, non-Gaussian, heavy-tailed coupling is a ubiquitous phenomenon in DNNs.

arxiv-2204-05919.title: Leveraging Reaction-aware Substructures for Retrosynthesis Analysis
arxiv-2204-05919.description: Abstract . Retrosynthesis analysis is a critical task in organic chemistry central to many important industries. Previously, various machine learning approaches have achieved promising results on this task by representing output molecules as strings and autoregressively decoded token-by-token with generative models. Text generation or machine translation models in natural language processing were frequently utilized approaches.

arxiv-2302-10561.title: Model-free Optimization and Experimental Validation of RIS-assisted Wireless Communications under Rich Multipath Fading Tianrui Chen and Minglei You are with University of Nottingham (Email: {Tianrui.Chen, Minglei.You}@nottingham.ac.uk), Gan Zheng is with University of Warwick (Email: gan.zheng@warw
arxiv-2302-10561.creator: Tianrui Chen, Minglei You, Yangyishi Zhang, Gan Zheng, Jean Baptiste Gros
arxiv-2302-10561.description: Abstract Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) devices have emerged as an effective way to control the propagation channels for enhancing the end-users’ performance. However, RIS optimization involves configuring the radio frequency response of a large number of radiating elements, which is challenging in real-world applications due to high computational complexity.

arxiv-2405-11845.title: Speed of Random Walks in Dirichlet Environment on a Galton-Watson Tree
arxiv-2405-11845.creator: Dongjian Qian, Yang Xiao
arxiv-2405-11845.description: Abstract This paper deals with a transient random walk in Dirichlet environment, or equivalently a linearly edge reinforced random walk, on a Galton-Watson tree. We compute the stationary distribution of the environment seen from the particle of an edge reinforced random walk.

arxiv-2408-06426.title: Semi-automatic Calculations of Multi-loop Feynman Amplitudes with AmpRed
arxiv-2408-06426.creator: Wen Chen
arxiv-2408-06426.description: Abstract We present a Mathematica package AmpRed for the semi-automatic calculations of multi-loop Feynman amplitudes with high efficiency and precision. AmpRed implements the methods of integration by parts and differential equations in the Feynman-parameter representation. It allows for the calculations of general parametric integrals (which may not have momentum-space correspondences).

arxiv-2408-10065.title: Stopping of very heavy ions in Mylar
arxiv-2408-10065.creator: R. N. Sagaidak
arxiv-2408-10065.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by R. N. Sagaidak. Available experimental data on Mylar stopping powers ( S ​ P SP s) for heavy ions (HIs) at energies 0.04 ⩽ E / A ⩽ 15 0.04\leqslant E/A\leqslant 15 MeV/nucleon have been compared to different semi-empirical model calculations with the aim of their possible usage for the estimates of ranges for very heavy ions at E / A < 0.5 E/A<0.5 MeV/nucleon, which are of practical interest.

arxiv-2410-21417.title: Nearly tight bounds for testing tree tensor network states
arxiv-2410-21417.creator: Benjamin Lovitz, Angus Lowe
arxiv-2410-21417.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Benjamin Lovitz, Angus Lowe. Tree tensor network states (TTNS) generalize the notion of having low Schmidt-rank to multipartite quantum states, through a parameter known as the bond dimension. This leads to succinct representations of quantum many-body systems with a tree-like entanglement structure. In this work, we study the task of testing whether an unknown pure state is a TTNS on n n qudits with bond dimension at most r r , or is far in trace distance from any such state.

arxiv-2509-08158.title: The Closest Point Heat Method for Solving Eikonal Equations on Implicit Surfaces
arxiv-2509-08158.creator: Tony WongShingyu Leung, Byungjoon Lee
arxiv-2509-08158.description: Abstract We introduce the Closest Point Heat Method (CPHM), a novel approach for solving the surface Eikonal equation on general smooth surfaces. Building on the strengths of the classical heat method, such as simplicity of implementation and computational efficiency, CPHM integrates closest point techniques to reduce dependence on surface meshes.

arxiv-2510-07395.title: Unified Spectrospatial Forward Models: Spatially Continuous Maps of Weak Emission Lines in the Rosette Nebula with SDSS-V LVM Astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2022 ) , CMasher ( van der Velden 2020 ) , Dask ( Dask Development Team 2016 ) , Equinox ( Kidger &

Méndez-Delgado, Andrew K. Saydjari, Luciano Vargas-Herrera, Niv Drory, Dmitry Bizyaev, José G. Fernández-Trincado, Carlos G. Román-Zúñiga, Juna A. Ko
arxiv-2510-07395.description: Abstract Analyses of IFU data are typically performed on a per-spaxel basis, with each spectrum modelled independently. For low signal-to-noise (S/N) features such as weak emission lines, estimating properties is difficult and imprecise. Arbitrary binning schemes boost S/N at the cost of resolution, and risk introducing biases.

arxiv-2510-18773.title: Detection and Simulation of Urban Heat Islands Using a Fine-Tuned Geospatial Foundation Model for Microclimate Impact Prediction
arxiv-2510-18773.creator: Jannis Fleckenstein, David Kreismann, Tamara Rosemary Govindasamy, Thomas Brunschwiler, Etienne Vos, Mattia Rigotti
arxiv-2510-18773.description: Abstract As urbanization and climate change progress, urban heat island effects are becoming more frequent and severe. To formulate effective mitigation plans, cities require detailed air temperature data, yet conventional machine learning models with limited data often produce inaccurate predictions, particularly in underserved areas.

arxiv-2512-02941.title: Pseudocodewords of quantum, quasi-cyclic, and spatially-coupled LDPC codes: a fundamental cone perspective Thanks: Matthews was partially supported by NSF DMS-2201075 and the Commonwealth Cyber Initiative. Thanks: McMillon was supported by NSF DMS-2303380 and partially supported by the Commonwealth
arxiv-2512-02941.creator: Wittawat Kositwattanarerk 1, Gretchen L. Matthews 2, Emily McMillon 2, Tunchanok Yutitumsatit 1
arxiv-2512-02941.description: Abstract . While low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes are near capacity-achieving when paired with iterative decoders, these decoders may not output a codeword due to the existence of pseudocodewords. Thus, pseudocodewords have been studied to give insight into the performance of modern decoders including iterative and linear programming decoders.

arxiv-2601-21790.title: Synthetic control over marcasite-pyrite polymorph formation in the Fe 1-x Co x Se 2 series
arxiv-2601-21790.creator: Luqman Mustafa, Susanne Kunzmann, Martin Kostka, Jill Fortmann, Aurelija Mockute, Alan Savan, Alfred Ludwig, Anna Grünebohm, Andreas Kreyssig, Anna E. Böhmer
arxiv-2601-21790.description: Abstract Transition-metal dichalcogenides of the pyrite-marcasite family are model systems of crystal chemistry. A few of these show polymorphism. The theoretical ground state of CoSe 2 is marcasite, but the material is typically synthesized in the pyrite structure. Polymorphism has been observed in nanoparticles and synthetic control of the polymorphs of CoSe 2 has not been achieved.

arxiv-2602-10403.title: Disability-First AI Dataset Annotation: Co-designing Stuttered Speech Annotation Guidelines with People Who Stutter Conference: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems; April 13–17, 2026; Barcelona, Spain Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in
arxiv-2602-10403.creator: Xinru Tang, Jingjin Li, Shaomei Wu
arxiv-2602-10403.description: Abstract . Despite efforts to increase the representation of disabled people in AI datasets, accessibility datasets are often annotated by crowdworkers without disability-specific expertise, leading to inconsistent or inaccurate labels. This paper examines these annotation challenges through a case study of annotating speech data from people who stutter (PWS).

pmc-10669203.title: Changes in Inner Retina Thickness and Macular Sensitivity in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes with Moderate Diabetic Retinopathy
pmc-10669203.creator: Ana Boned-Murillo, Guisela Fernández-Espinosa, Elvira Orduna-Hospital, Maria Dolores Díaz-Barreda, Ana Sánchez-Cano, María Sopeña-Pinilla, Sofía Bielsa-Alonso, Isabel Pinilla
pmc-10669203.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The increase in diabetic retinopathy (DR) prevalence demonstrates the need for the determination of biomarkers for assessing disease development to obtain an early diagnosis and stop its progression. We aimed to analyse total retinal (RT) and inner retinal layer (IRL) thicknesses in type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM2) patients and correlate these results with retinal sensitivity using swept-source OCT (SS-OCT) and microperimetry.

pmc-12458715.title: Independent and joint relationships of physical activity and pulmonary function with the risk of all-cause mortality
pmc-12458715.creator: Jingxin Ma, Can Shen, Yu Jia, Rong Yang, Shanye Yi, Yiheng Zhou, Rui Zeng, Zhi Wan, Qian Zhao, Yi Lei, Xiaoyang Liao
pmc-12458715.description: BackgroundPhysical activity (PA) plays a crucial protective role in the overall health outcomes of individuals with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. However, accurate recommendations for amount and categories of PA are still unclear for individuals with impaired pulmonary function (PF) in community environments. Thus, this study aims to investigate the independent and joint relationships of PA and PF with mortality.

pmc-12491037.title: Is vigorous physical activity effective for preventing kidney stones?
pmc-12491037.creator: Yuanfu Wang, Qing Wei, Yue Dai, Sisi Chen, Bo Cheng
pmc-12491037.description: BackgroundWith a high rate of occurrence and recurrence, kidney stones represent a common urological issue that poses a substantial burden on public health infrastructures globally. While prior research has linked poor diet and lifestyle to a heightened susceptibility to kidney stones, the impact of daily vigorous physical activity (VPA) duration on kidney stone incidence remains under-investigated.

pmc-12797603.title: Violacein: a natural antibacterial agent empowered by film-forming sprays for topical applications
pmc-12797603.creator: Kampanart Huanbutta, Pornsak Sriamornsak, Parapat Sobharaksha, Natta Thuphabut, Chaiyawat Rachagrai, Narabhorn Sangnak, Suwisit Manmuan, Tanikan Sangnim
pmc-12797603.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectiveThe rise of antibiotic-resistant microorganisms poses a significant public health threat. Exploring natural compounds with antibacterial properties offers a potential solution. Violacein, derived from Chromobacterium violaceum, has shown promise for its antibacterial and antioxidant effects. This study aims to develop and evaluate a violacein-loaded film-forming spray (FFS) to enhance patient adherence through a flexible, peelable skin film, while maintaining antibacterial efficacy.MethodsThe antibacterial and antioxidant activities of violacein crude extract were evaluated.

pmc-13287392.creator: Halle Walls, Cassidy Shields, Matthew Ellington, Eric Edmonds
pmc-13287392.description: Background:First rib fractures are an infrequently encountered injury, especially in the young athlete. Incidence and natural history of those with first rib fractures sustained during sport is poorly elucidated in the literature, contributing to variability of treatment of this injury.

pmc-13474059.title: Role of Life’s Essential 8 in the association of night shift work with cardiovascular disease and mortality: a prospective cohort study of UK Biobank participants
pmc-13474059.creator: Yeen Huang, Yingping Xiang, Tianzheng Li, Gregory Yoke Hong Lip, Yanhui Gao, Junguo Zhang
pmc-13474059.description: BackgroundNight shift work is linked to higher risks of cardiovascular disease (CVD) and mortality, but mechanisms remain unclear. Lifestyle, captured by the American Heart Association’s Life’s Essential 8 (LE8), may act as a modifiable mediator. We aimed to examine the associations of night shift work with CVD and mortality and quantify the mediating role of LE8.
